title: How does a switch learn MAC addresses?
question: How does a switch learn MAC addresses?
answer: A switch learns MAC addresses dynamically. When a frame arrives, the switch records the frame's source MAC address and the port it arrived on in its MAC address table (also called the CAM table), with a timestamp. For forwarding, it looks up the destination MAC: if the address is known, the frame is sent only out of the matching port; if it is unknown, or the destination is a broadcast/multicast address, the frame is flooded out of all ports in the same VLAN except the ingress port. Table entries age out after a default of 300 seconds.
